reviews.text: We came here a couple of days ago for the first time as our dog Lola was ill and her main vet clinic is further out. They explained everything very thoroughly and made Lola feel more at ease, she has been getting better since the visit.The price of the visit and everything she had to have was not as high as I thought it was going to be.  We will definitely be back if we need a trusted clinic nearby!

​I honestly don’t even know how to properly thank the team at Sherbourne Animal Hospital, but I need people to know what they did for me.
​My dog Astrid is a senior German Shepherd/Border Collie mix, and she’s been my entire world since 2015. A few Sundays ago, she suddenly started bleeding out. It happened so fast. I panicked, threw her in the car, and rushed her to the only emergency clinic I could find open. They took one look and quoted me a price for life-saving surgery that was just crushingly far beyond what I could afford. I was faced with the absolute nightmare of having to euthanize my best friend simply because I didn't have the money. Even their fee just to put her to sleep was astronomical.
​I left that clinic completely broken. It’s a sickening feeling—walking out into the daylight seeing everyone else just going about their normal lives, while your own is falling apart. Astrid looked up at me with these eyes that seemed to say, Please help me, and it absolutely killed me.
​I drove over to Sherbourne Animal Hospital, and my only plan was to see if they could at least affordably help her cross the rainbow bridge. I walked up to the front desk, completely defeated, and just broke down crying as I told the receptionist my story. I was entirely convinced this was the last hour I would ever spend with Astrid.
​But the receptionist didn’t just slide a clipboard across the counter with euthanasia paperwork. She just looked at me and said, "Give me one second. Please, don't sign anything yet."
​She disappeared into the back. I stood in that lobby for what felt like a lifetime, just mentally preparing to say my final goodbye.
​Then, one of the veterinarians came out. She didn't bring paperwork. She came out to tell me that she had just made a call, and they work with a local community church fund for veterinary emergencies. They were going to step in. They were going to cover the cost of part her surgery.
​They didn't just process my grief. They went to work and saved her life.
​I walked into that clinic preparing to say my final goodbye to my best friend. Instead, these extraordinary people handed her back to me. I went in asking for a merciful ending, and they gave us more time. I will never be able to thank them enough.

If you had asked me a week ago, I would have said I loved Sherbourne Animal Clinic. Up until recently, my dog Penny never had any serious health issues, and I trusted the clinic completely.

However, after what has happened, I can no longer recommend them.
I brought Penny in twice in April 2025: first on April 8th because she was showing signs of soreness, and then again on April 17th for her annual vaccines. Both times, they supposedly performed a full wellness check. Despite this, they completely missed a serious anal gland issue that just days later ruptured and required emergency treatment.

This situation could have been easily prevented with a proper, thorough exam like a wellness check is supposed to provide. It is now my understanding that anal gland issues are extremely common in small breed dogs, yet at no point over the two years I visited this clinic was I ever educated about this risk or the need for regular checks.

If you are looking for veterinary services in the downtown area, I strongly recommend going instead to Toronto Central Animal Clinic at Parliament and Adelaide. They are open seven days a week, they actually take the time to follow up on your pet’s care, and the follow-up calls are made by the vet himself, not just the front desk staff. I immediately felt the difference in the level of care and attention my dog received there.

The vets at Sherbourne Animal Clinic seem kind, but when it comes to thorough, proactive animal care, I unfortunately can no longer trust or recommend them based on my experience.

Our otherwise healthy 2.5 year old cat had been vomiting frequently, so we took her in to get checked out. Physical exam went fine so they put her on a round of Famotidine, and told us to call if it didn’t improve after a couple of weeks.

It didn’t, so we went back and had imaging done. We were informed that the imaging showed a foreign body in her stomach, so she was given a laxative gel to see if she was able to pass it. She did not, so we were given a requisition for an endoscopy at a third-party clinic.

A week or so after waiting to hear back from the other clinic, she was still vomiting frequently so we opted to take her to an emergency vet hospital.

They performed an ultrasound and endoscopy which revealed there was no foreign body in her stomach, but a mass on her pancreas as well as gallstones. Unfortunately this meant the mass had gone untreated for two months, and it had done significant irreparable damage to other organs. This led to us having to make the difficult decision to let her pass peacefully. Had the initial imaging diagnosis been correct, we could have treated the actual issue and she would likely still be with us today.

The front desk staff and vet we dealt with were lovely, but I would not trust them with my other cat’s care after this experience.
